differences.reason: With JavaScript blocked the page runs no script in Chrome or the shell, but Electron fails the extension's MAIN world script ("Script not run") where Chrome returns a null result.

Chrome shows chrome.userScripts only after the person turns on "Allow User Scripts" for the extension; PeerSky has no such switch yet and people rely on user script managers, so it is on unless the host's isUserScriptsAllowed hook says no.

Electron gives an extension file access only when the host loads it with allowFileAccess, which the shell cannot read back, so it answers false unless the host's isFileSchemeAccessAllowed hook says yes, where Chrome lets an unpacked extension read files.
